stem.text: The passage outlines the endocrine system.
Complete the passage by using the most appropriate scientific terms.

The endocrine system consists of tissues and ................................................................. ,
which secrete hormones such as insulin, glucagon and antidiuretic hormone (ADH).
Glucagon only affects target cells that have complementary receptors, which are located
on the ................................................................. . Glucagon binds to these receptors
and this leads to the production of a ................................................................. , which
transfers the signal throughout the cytoplasm. The target cells for insulin are in the liver,
................................................................. and adipose tissue. The target cells for ADH are
those of the distal convoluted tubule and the ................................................................. of the
kidney nephron. These hormones are involved in ................................................................. ,
which is the maintenance of a constant internal environment.

points.text: cell surface membrane / plasma membrane ; A liver (cells)
second messenger / cAMP ; A enzyme cascade / phosphorylation of enzymes / signalling cascade

explanation.text: Endocrine glands release hormones that act only on cells with suitable receptors. Glucagon signalling uses a second messenger, while the hormone targets link endocrine coordination to homeostasis.

reasoningChain: Use the hormone and target-cell context to identify each blank.
Distinguish membrane receptors from intracellular second messengers.

inferredMistakes.text: Placing the glucagon receptor inside the nucleus.

stem.text: The blood glucose concentration of a person was measured at regular intervals after the ingestion of a meal rich in glucose.
Fig. 9.1 shows the results of this investigation.

stem.caption: Fig. 9.1
stem.alt: Blood glucose concentration after a glucose-rich meal, with phases A and B and a set point.

stem.text: Explain how the blood glucose concentration is reduced during phase A of the curve.

points.text: increase in uptake of glucose into cells ;
detail of uptake ; e.g. increase permeability of cell surface membrane (to glucose) / GLUT added to cell surface membrane
increase / stimulates, respiration of glucose (in cells) / phosphorylation of glucose ;
(stimulates) glycogenesis / conversion of glucose to lipids ;

explanation.text: Raised blood glucose stimulates insulin release. Insulin promotes glucose entry and use or storage, so blood glucose returns towards the set point.

reasoningChain: Identify the hormone responding to raised glucose.
Link uptake, respiration and glycogenesis to the decrease.

inferredMistakes.text: Using glucagon to explain the fall in blood glucose.

stem.text: Suggest why the blood glucose concentration increases again during phase B.

explanation.text: A fall below the set point stimulates glucagon release, leading to glucose release by the liver.

reasoningChain: Identify glucagon as the corrective hormone.

inferredMistakes.text: Naming insulin as the hormone raising blood glucose in phase B.
